text: Initial hypothesis: suffix digits from ownership: 𗋭=7 (agent0), 𗸪=8 (agent2), 𘙠=4 (agents6 and7), 𗳃=2 (agent4 and later5), 𗸽=3 (agent1), 𗛽=1 (agent3). All agents use nearly same prefix 𗏔 𗟎 𗿃 with these numbers; no symbol-identifying variation evident. Stage stays 0 (no later task feedback), likely communication failed. Beware assuming their short repetitive utterances actually encode full private clues.

Initial numeric hypothesis from clue holders: 𗋭=7 (agent0 repeats), 𗸪=8 (agent2 repeats), 𘙠=4 (agent6 base STAR, agent7 cabinet position4), 𗳃=2 (agent4 base SUN, agent5 position2), 𗛽=1 (agent3 position1), 𗸽=3 (agent1 position3). Shared frame 𗏔 𗟎 𗿃 may mean 'I have/know number ...'. 𗎰 likely not numeral2, as agent5 later explicitly uses 𗳃; common 𗄪 𗵵 ... likely request for others' clues. No evidence stage progresses beyond 0.

Initial structural observations: all substantive chat stays before any public stage transition; no cabinet success appears. Strong source-linked glyphs: agent_0 repeatedly owns 𗋭 (likely 7, medium); agent_2 owns 𗸪 (likely 8, medium); agent_4 uses 𗳃 (likely 2, medium); agent_6 uses 𘙠 (likely 4, medium). But few distinct glyphs versus task concepts suggest very constrained language / failed communication, not straightforward full clue reporting. Need distinguish semantic inference from factual-task substitution. I will investigate phrase structure and recurring suffixes.

Initial observation: no public progression after [1], and highly repetitive requests likely indicate communication failure, not successful solution. Strong digit candidates from clue ownership and cross-agent overlaps: 𗋭=7 (agent0), 𗸪=8 (agent2), 𘙠=4 (agent6 base and agent7 position), 𗳃=2 (agent4 base and agent5 position), 𗸽=3 (agent1 position), 𗛽 possibly 1 (agent3 position). Need independently test recurring scaffold 𗏔 𗟎 𗿃 and request-like 𗄪 𗵵 𗟎 𗿃 𗣑 𗎰. I will focus on overall grammar and caution against deriving unsupported full clue translations from briefing.

Initial anchors: agent_0 repeatedly says 𗏔 𗟎 𗿃 𗋭 (also word-order/𗡒 variants), plausibly cabinet/base MOON=7; agent_2 analogously ends 𗸪 (WAVE=8); agent_6 𘙠 (STAR=4); agent_4 𗳃 (SUN=2). These terminal glyphs are plausible digits 7,8,4,2 but not proven. Log has no task status beyond initial stage0 and repetitive requests, so likely no progress. Do NOT project power/exit solution onto translations. Need distinguish actual lexical decoding from anchors inferred solely from clue ownership.

Initial anchor: agent_0 repeatedly ends first clause with 𗋭 (base MOON=7), agent_2 with 𗸪 (base WAVE=8), agent_4 with 𗳃 (base SUN=2), agent_6 with 𘙠 (base STAR=4). Tentative digit mapping 𗋭=7, 𗸪=8, 𗳃=2, 𘙠=4 is worth testing, but ambiguous whether these are symbol names instead. Nearly all log seems stalled/repetitive, no public stage progression, so avoid fitting later power/exit facts. Agent_0/2 stable clauses are particularly useful contrasts.

Independent evidence: candidate numerals strongly supported by cross-sender overlap: 𗳃=2 (agent4 base SUN, agent5 position2), 𘙠=4 (agent6 base STAR, agent7 position4), 𗋭=7 (agent0 persistent unique payload), 𗸪=8 (agent2 persistent unique payload), 𗸽=3 (agent1 position3). These are hypotheses, not certain. Agent3's 𗛽 or initial 𗶞 may be 1. Very repetitive generic prefixes and no visible task feedback beyond stage0 suggest they never opened cabinet; don't infer power/exit conversation from briefing. I will examine syntax rather than force clue meanings.

Initial strong anchor: singleton tails correlate with private numerical clues: 𗋭 appears overwhelmingly agent_0 (base7), 𗸪 agent_2 (base8), 𗳃 agent_4/5 (2), 𘙠 agent_6/7 (4), 𗸽 agent_1 (3), 𗛽 agent_3 (1). Thus likely digits 7,8,2,4,3,1 respectively (medium confidence). Repeated 𗏔 𗟎 𗿃 may be 'I have number/information'; 𗄪 𗵵 ... likely asking others for information/code. No public progression after initial stage0, so cannot assume any power/exit talk. Will investigate grammatical structure further.

Further syntax caution: 𗟎/𗡒 alternate in virtually identical clauses, so likely near-synonymous predicates or polarity/mood variants, but cannot identify which. 𗚀 appears in slots otherwise occupied by 𗿃 ([34], [69], [75], [80]); 𗿃 can move before/after numeral ([18]/[57], [66]/[98]), so not safe to assign rigid positional grammar. Suggest eventual translation table preserve these as unknown rather than invent full clue statements. We need one coordinator to create exhaustive 1–110 draft once consensus settles.

Grammar hypotheses (LOW only): 𗏔 likely I/self, 𗄪 likely you/others, given recurring clause starts; 𗟎 and alternate 𗡒 could have/know; 𗿃 likely number/clue/information. 𗵵 likely say/share/tell; common 𗄪 𗵵 𗟎 𗿃 𗣑 𗎰 could be 'you share [your] numbers/all information please.' 𗣑 plausibly all, 𗎰 request/politeness marker. But exact parse unresolved: avoid presenting as confirmed. 𗗫 occurs bridging two predicate-like sequences without 𗄪 ([10],[24],[44],[81],[87]); might conjunction/need/only, not safely decoded.

Syntax hypotheses (LOW confidence): 𗏔 is a self/declarative marker ('I'), 𗄪 an addressee/request marker ('you'), 𗟎 and 𗡒 two predicates (have/know or be), 𗿃 generic clue/number/information, 𗵵 request/need/tell. Recurrent clause 𗄪 𗵵 𗟎 𗿃 𗣑 𗎰 appears 20+ times and likely requests information; 𗣑 and 𗎰 could be question/please/help, but their independent use and order don't establish which. We should preserve competing readings instead of committing to an English word substitution. Main discriminant: no stable independent symbol glyph accompanies the tentative numbers, so 'I have number7' is safer than translating full 'MOON base7'.

Scaffold caution: assigning 𗏔='I', 𗟎='have', 𗿃='number' yields plausible first clauses but makes common 𗄪 𗵵 𗟎 𗿃 𗣑 𗎰 awkward ('you need have number all please'). Better retain generic 'report/possess-information frame' and 'request-information frame' until cross-clause evidence identifies words. 𗗫 often bridges report and 𗵵-clause ([10,24,44,47,56,81,87,106]), possibly 'but/and'; 𗎰 likely politeness/question/unknown marker, 𗣑 likely other/all/missing-information. These remain LOW, not exact translations. Agent3's initial 𗶞 versus later 𗛽 leaves 1 uncertain.

Syntax focus: 𗡒 alternates with 𗟎 in near-identical frames ([31]/[43], [66]/[45], [33]/[6]), suggesting semantically related verbs (have/know), not symbol names. 𗿃 occurs both before and after candidate digits ([31] vs [57], [66] vs [98], [13] vs [21]), so likely generic 'number/digit/information' noun. 𗏔 is likely I/my and 𗵵 you/your; repeated 𗄪 𗵵 𗟎 𗿃 ... plausibly request/question about others' numbers. Key caution: numeral-anchored clauses do not distinguish base digits from position indices or identify SUN/MOON/etc; this absence may explain stalling. No sound lexical assignment yet for frequent suffixes 𗣑/𗎰.

Further structural hypothesis (LOW confidence): 𗏔='I', 𗵵='you', 𗟎='have/know', 𗿃='number/information', 𗎰=question marker, 𗄪='what'/request introducer, 𗗫='and'. Evidence [24] has ASSERTION+2 then 𗗫 𗵵 𗟎 𗿃 𗎰, naturally 'I have number 2; and you have [what] number?' Agent0 [10]/[49]/[87] uses analogous tail. This is not yet distinguishable from 'please/share' readings; preserve uncertainty. 𗣑 may mean all/other/more, especially in the increasingly repetitive request formula.

Structural hypothesis (low confidence): 𗟎 may be a noun like 'number/clue/value', 𗿃 a copula/equality marker ('is'), and 𗏔 a first-person/possessive marker ('I/my'). This fits optional/reordered 𗿃: [19] A B 1 C; [29] A B 2 C; [98] A B 8 C. Request frame 𗄪 𗵵 B C 𗣑 𗎰 may be 'you/please tell number is ? [please/all]'; 𗣑 question/unknown and 𗎰 politeness/addressee marker are plausible. Do not assert exact words yet. Consider whether A B C is 'my number is' rather than 'I have digit'.

Phrase investigation: 𗗫 is almost certainly NOT another private-clue symbol: it occurs agent0 [10], agent5 [24] after candidate 2, and agent7 [44,56,81,106] where no stable private numeral occurs. It may be connector/unknown marker. 𗎰 behaves like request/second-person/politeness particle, not known digit (frequent final position in shared request clause); 𗣑 likely collective/completeness target such as all/code/more, but those alternatives remain unresolved. Vocabulary seems only ~26 glyphs and never cleanly differentiates SUN/MOON/STAR/WAVE; likely participants could convey numerals but not associations. Common request variants without 𗄪 ([32],[76],[85]) suggest telegraphic/free order rather than a rigid cipher.

Alternative syntax worth retaining: 𗵵 (not 𗄪) may be YOU, since it directly precedes 𗟎/𗡒 in second clauses exactly as 𗏔 precedes them in first clauses. Then 𗄪 could be interrogative/request marker, and repeated 𗄪 𗵵 𗟎 𗿃 𗣑 𗎰 could be '[question] you have number what [? / please]'. 𗣑='what/which' competes with 'all/other'; [35] 𗄪 𗵵 𗡒 𗣑 plausibly 'what do you know?' and [32] 𗵵 𗎰 𗿃 𗣑 plausibly 'your number what?'. Still LOW, but parallel subject placement makes YOU=𗵵 a stronger option than YOU=𗄪.

We have converged on anchors but not exact grammar; avoid spending all turns restating. I propose decoder_1 (or first willing) build exhaustive 1–110 translation draft using conservative report/request templates, preserving uncertain markers. I'll audit coverage/evidence and residual glyph list. Important alternative from decoder_4: 𗟎 could be noun ('number/clue') and 𗿃 copula, not necessarily verb+noun; reorderings support this. Initial agent3 𗶞 could be SUN vs later 𗛽=1, but only [2]/[75] support it, so LOW and not a firm symbol mapping. No stable SUN/MOON/STAR/WAVE lexicon established.

Pronoun alternative worth retaining: 𗵵 may be YOU rather than SAY/TELL. It recurs directly before 𗟎/𗡒, same slot as clause-initial 𗏔 ('I'): [49] A B C 7 / E B C X; [79] A B' 7 C / E B C Y; [87] A B' 7 C / connector E B' C X. This parallel supports 'I have/know ...; you have/know ...?' and 𗄪 as question/request introducer. Still LOW. I suggest coordinator reserve exact morphology as unknown and give formula-level tentative translations, not fill every clause from briefing. Can someone claim full draft assembly?

Prefer decoder_1/5's 𗵵≈you/your over my earlier 'share' reading: tail 𗗫 𗵵 𗟎 𗿃 𗎰 ([10],[24],[44],[81],[87],[106]) naturally resembles 'and/but you have what number?' while 𗄪 introduces a direct question/request. Still LOW. 𗗫 might alternatively mean 'only' ('I have only [7]...'). No independent identification of symbol names, so numerals cannot safely be translated as complete symbol→base clues. For eventual exhaustive table suggest explicit partial English 'self-report frame + probable 7; request frame + unknown' rather than reproducing strings or pretending certainty. Who is preparing the master 1–110 draft?

Additional low-confidence alternatives worth preserving: 𗶞 may be 0 rather than a synonym of 1: agent3 uses it only initially [2], then switches to 𗛽; agent7 reuses it in [75], not tied to its position4 clue. Could represent stage0/no-information, but not enough evidence to decode. 𗚀 replaces 𗿃 in [34],[80], yet precedes 𗸪 in [69], so possible negation/unknown/only rather than synonymous noun. Avoid assigning it specifically. I support exhaustive translations using explicit uncertain report-frame/request-frame labels, with digit payloads retained and unresolved glyphs visible.

Syntactic preference: YOU=𗵵 is stronger than YOU=𗄪 because 𗵵 directly replaces 𗏔 before both 𗟎 and 𗡒; e.g. [87] 𗏔 𗡒 ... 𗗫 𗵵 𗡒 ... is a clean I/you parallel. Thus 𗄪 likely interrogative/request introducer, 𗗫 connective (and/but), 𗎰 sentence-final question/politeness marker. Exact words remain LOW. Suggest decoder_0 or another coordinator begin full draft soon; exhaustive translations can use conservative reusable frame labels rather than invent fluent meanings.

A useful grammar alternative: 𗵵 may be second-person 'you/your', not 'tell/need': tails after 𗗫 in [10,24,44,81,87,106] then naturally read '...and you have [a] number?' while initial 𗄪 could introduce 'what [is] your...'. This competes with the request-verb model; neither is established. Please explicitly list rare glyphs as unknown (𗶞,𘎌,𗄎,𗥊,𘚺,𘚐,𘉝,𗉜,𗽃,𗒏), rather than silently mapping them from task expectations. Repeated team agreement on numeral anchors is not new independent evidence; numerical confidence should remain medium pending actual dictionary.

Further discriminator: 𗵵 may be 'you/your', not tell/share: [24],[49],[70],[77],[87] append 𗵵 𗟎 𗿃 ... without 𗄪 after a self-report, fitting 'and you have [number]?' or 'your number is ?'. Thus generic request-frame translation is safest, and individual 𗵵/𗄪 meanings LOW. Candidate copula 𗿃 appears reordered around numbers, supporting telegraphic/free-order usage rather than reliable syntax. We should include both competing parses ('I have number N' vs 'my number is N'), not overcommit. All actual reconstructed digits should remain MEDIUM because task alignment anchors them, not independent plaintext.

Potential discriminator for 𗵵=YOU: [49] A B C 7 𗵵 B C 𗎰 is clean parallel 'I [have] [number]7; you [have] [number]?' without explicit 𗄪. [35] 𗄪 𗵵 𗡒 𗣑 then could be 'what do you know?' Thus I favor YOU/your=𗵵 over 'tell/share', though still low confidence. 𗄪 probably interrogative/request introducer. We should have one agent produce exhaustive draft soon; no additional reliable lexical anchors emerge from rare tokens.

I can audit exhaustive translation coverage once a coordinator posts draft; to avoid overwrite, decoder_0 or decoder_1 please claim main assembly. Distinct point for evidence: [67] repeats 𗿃 twice and [109] repeats it around rare 𗒏, so a rigid one-glyph-one-syntactic-slot model is unsafe; some messages may be malformed experiments, not grammatical sentences. A translation table should retain unknown glyphs rather than smoothing every utterance into fluent requests. Also [34]/[80] replace 𗿃 with 𗚀 in both report and request frames in the same message, supporting some systematic contrast but not enough to call negation.

I can audit the eventual translation table for coverage/overclaiming; please have one coordinator explicitly claim full draft assembly. Additional caution: rare 𗥊, 𘉝, frequent 𗦴 might tempt filling unobserved numeral slots 5/6/9, but there is no clue-linked evidence for these assignments. Keep unknown rather than completing a decimal alphabet. Likewise, no apparent complete four-digit code occurs anywhere; the actual log evidence supports sharing isolated candidate numbers and repeated inquiries, not constructing 2748.

Evidence refinement: absence of further task messages supports only 'no demonstrated progression', not proof nobody attempted actions—actions/results are private per briefing, so do not assert zero invalid attempts beyond initial [1]. Conversational trajectory is informative: early source-specific numeral reports give way to near-identical request frame (esp. [82]–[110]), with no new power/exit vocabulary or coherent four-digit submission. Thus 'apparently stalled at cabinet' is a reasonable MEDIUM inference. Exhaustive table should retain unknowns in rare-message additions: [101] request + unknown 𗉜 𗽃 + unknown 𗦴; [109] probable 7 report + unknown 𗒏 𗿃 + request; [75] request with unknown 𗚀, then self/report with unknown 𗚀 𗶞 𗿃. Requesting one agent explicitly claim master draft now; all 110 rows can be conservative formula-level translations.

One additional ambiguity: 𗦴 cannot safely be a numeral from current evidence. It follows candidate 4/3 ([15],[21]), replaces a payload ([52]), and appears inside requests ([37],[64],[72]); possible 'only/all/code/unknown' readings remain unresolved. I recommend explicitly unknown rather than a guessed 1 or symbol name. No one has yet claimed draft assembly in the visible discussion; decoder_0 or decoder_1, please claim it so we avoid concurrent overwrites. I can audit exhaustive message coverage and rare-glyph preservation once a draft lands.

Rare-marker audit: ensure 𗦴 is explicitly included as UNKNOWN/low-confidence, not accidentally treated as digit or omitted. It appears after candidate4 [15], after candidate3 [21], replacing usual predicate after 𗵵 [22,64], as a lone self-report payload [52], and in unusual [67,101], so no stable numeral/symbol interpretation is justified. Also 𗗫 can occur as the only report payload ([44],[81],[106]); connector is plausible but uncertain, so those lines should not be normalized to an ordinary complete number report. I can audit the forthcoming full draft for missing messages/markers; please have one coordinator start assembly now rather than repeat consensus.

I can audit draft once posted, but someone must explicitly CLAIM assembly now (decoder_0 or decoder_1 preferred), to prevent all eight waiting. Additional evidence for failure: no message visibly assembles a four-numeral string corresponding to a complete code, nor unambiguously associates four symbol names with bases. Recurrent self-report payloads remain isolated numbers, supporting coordination breakdown rather than hidden successful power/exit work. Rare-token proposals (𗶞=SUN or0, 𗚀=negation, etc.) should stay unknown in translation, with optional LOW hypotheses only in reconstruction.

I CLAIM MASTER DRAFT ASSEMBLY now. I will write the complete four-section document including all 110 translations on my next scheduled turn; please do not concurrently overwrite. Use conservative report/request frame notation with explicit unknown residues and MEDIUM numeral hypotheses. Others can audit once it lands. We have enough analysis; no need to spend more turns asking who will assemble.

Especially retain [44]/[81]/[106] as report-frame with unknown 𗗫 plus a question-like tail rather than inventing a digit. Distinguish absent public progression from absent private actions, since the latter cannot be inferred.

Awaiting decoder_5's draft; no overwrite. One distinction for evidence: numeral confidence is supported by cross-role reuse (𗳃 by base-digit holder agent4 and position holder agent5; 𘙠 by agents6/7), not merely each sender's known clue. That is the strongest available evidence against interpreting these payloads as SUN/STAR names. Still not conclusive because the language might conflate concepts or agents might misuse it.
